task: Repair ONLY the invalid-input/batch-isolation defect that an independent NEW CHAT hostile review of commit c90c54b established (BLOCK verdict): a gzip-valid raw object whose decompressed body is not valid UTF-8 raised an uncaught UnicodeDecodeError out of materialize_parser_a(), which terminated materialize_batch() before later objects in the same batch were attempted. Does not touch OHLC, duplicate, timestamp, event-order, schema, or lifecycle logic in either parser; does not repair the separately-noted, still-open unknown-schema A/B divergence.

independent_review_blocker.reproducer: bad_utf8 = b'\xff\xfe\x00invalid utf8 csv content\n'; raw = gzip.compress(bad_utf8); materialize_parser_a(raw, date(2023,11,14), 'x') raised UnicodeDecodeError uncaught instead of returning a MaterializationResult
independent_review_blocker.root_cause: qntylab/r1_reference_parser.py:_decompress() calls .decode('utf-8', errors='strict') OUTSIDE its own GzipCorruptionError try/except block, so an invalid-UTF-8 decompressed body escapes parse_daily_object() as a bare UnicodeDecodeError rather than being wrapped as GzipCorruptionError. materialize_parser_a() (as introduced by c90c54b) only caught (GzipCorruptionError, TruncatedCSVError), not UnicodeDecodeError.
independent_review_blocker.batch_isolation_consequence: in materialize_batch(items, materialize_parser_a), an invalid-UTF-8 object at any position terminated the loop; subsequent valid objects were never attempted -- reproduced directly with a valid/corrupt/valid fixture (object C, which would materialize MATERIALIZED_VALID_RECORD, was never reached).
independent_review_blocker.parser_b_was_unaffected: materialize_parser_b's own _decode_container() (introduced by c90c54b) already caught UnicodeDecodeError explicitly and converted it to CONTAINER_ANOMALY; only the Parser A path had the gap.
independent_review_blocker.reason_c90c54b_was_not_population_ready: a single corrupted raw object of this shape, encountered anywhere in a real batch materialized through the Parser A path, would silently drop every subsequent object in that batch from the attempted set with no typed record and no exception surfaced to the caller as a per-object failure -- an unacceptable evidence-loss failure mode for population-scale materialization.
independent_review_blocker.docstring_accuracy_finding: the review additionally found that _decode_container's docstring claimed to mirror parse_daily_object's own container-decoding classification 'exactly (same exception classes...)', which was not literally true given the root cause above. Corrected in this repair (see below); no semantic behavior claim was walked back, only the exception-class-identity claim.

repair_implementation.change: extended the except tuple around the rp.parse_daily_object(...) call from (rp.GzipCorruptionError, rp.TruncatedCSVError) to (rp.GzipCorruptionError, rp.TruncatedCSVError, UnicodeDecodeError); all three map to the same, already-frozen CONTAINER_ANOMALY / MATERIALIZATION_QUARANTINED_NO_RECORD outcome already used for the other two classes. No new anomaly vocabulary introduced.
repair_implementation.not_a_generic_catch_all: the except tuple remains a fixed, explicit, three-member list of authorized object-corruption exception classes, not `except Exception`. Verified by two dedicated regression tests (test_materialize_parser_a_does_not_swallow_unrelated_exceptions, test_materialize_parser_b_does_not_swallow_unrelated_exceptions) that monkeypatch the underlying parser call to raise an unrelated RuntimeError and assert it still propagates uncaught through both materialize_parser_a and materialize_parser_b.
repair_implementation.parser_files_not_edited: qntylab/r1_reference_parser.py and qntylab/r1_retention_candidate.py were NOT modified; their SHA-256 hashes are byte-identical to before this task (see parser_hashes below). The root cause (the un-wrapped .decode() call in r1_reference_parser.py:_decompress) is compensated for at the boundary/call-site level in r1_daily_market_materializer.py, not fixed inside Parser A's own file, per this task's explicit constraint.
repair_implementation.docstrings_corrected: module docstring (concern #3), materialize_parser_a()'s docstring, and _decode_container()'s docstring were all updated to describe the actual architecture: _decode_container() reaches the identical outcome classification as parse_daily_object but not via an identical internal exception path, because Parser A's own _decompress() leaves the UnicodeDecodeError case un-wrapped; materialize_parser_a() compensates for that specific gap at its own call site rather than claiming exact mirroring.
